findings.title: Output more than doubled, at the same pace everywhere
findings.text: Papers grew 11.9% / 11.1% / 11.7% a year (IIITA / ABV / IIITB, log-linear fit 2016–2025, all p < 0.001): IIITA 174→374, ABV 126→332, IIITB 77→184 papers.

findings.title: Quality rose with quantity
findings.text: The Q1 share of journal papers rose from 30.2% to 44.2% at IIITA and from 26.2% to 40.8% at ABV between 2016–19 and 2022–25 (χ², p < 0.001). IIITB already started high (42.5% → 54.6%, p = 0.076), so growth did not come at the cost of venue quality.

findings.title: Raw citations exaggerate the gap between institutes
findings.text: IIITB's median paper has 2 citations vs 4 at IIITA, but 70% of its output is conference papers. Normalised for year, field and type, mean impact is 1.048 (ABV), 1.013 (IIITA) and 0.901 (IIITB, 95% CI 0.828–0.98): a modest, not a large, difference.

findings.title: Impact is carried by a few papers
findings.text: Citation Gini is 0.733–0.778; the top 10% of papers collect 57.9–63.4% of all citations. Among core faculty the top 20% write 42.6–55.2% of papers, and output and h-index move together (Spearman ρ = 0.871).

findings.title: The 'international premium' is really a venue and team-size effect
findings.text: Internationally co-authored papers score 1.242 vs 0.941 for single-institute papers (Mann–Whitney p < 0.001). Once venue, type, team size, year and field are held fixed (OLS, n = 5,087), the international effect is +2% (n.s.), while a Q1 venue adds +137%, a conference venue -51%, and doubling the team +27%.

findings.title: Internal citation is almost entirely self-citation
findings.text: 94.0% of the 5,946 citations between papers of the three institutes share an author, and 97.4% stay inside the citing institute versus 40.3% expected when targets are shuffled (z = 97.1). Only 355 links connect different research groups, so internal PageRank mostly measures group continuity rather than cross-group influence.

findings.title: Three islands: tight groups, almost no IIIT–IIIT collaboration
findings.text: The co-authorship network is small-world (clustering 0.691 vs 0.0016 random, path length 5.47 vs 4.9) and strongly modular (Q = 0.868 vs 0.45 ± 0.0016 in degree-preserving random graphs). Institute assortativity is 0.949: only 37 papers link two of the three IIITs. Core faculty have a median of 18 co-authors vs 3 for others.

findings.title: Citations follow collaboration, not topic overlap
findings.text: Institutes that co-author more with us also cite us more (Spearman ρ = 0.669 / 0.691 / 0.579, all p < 0.001). Co-author partners are about a third of the Indian institutes that cite us but supply 57.0–72.5% of those citations. Topic similarity does not predict who we collaborate with (ρ = 0.102, p = 0.59).

findings.title: From citation importers to exporters
findings.text: Per year, ABV has received more citations from other Indian institutes than it gives since 2022 and IIITA since 2023; IIITB is still below parity (2025 ratio 0.921). Summed over 2016–2026, IIITA (0.936) and ABV (0.971) are near balance while IIITB (0.691) remains a net importer of Indian citations.
